name: Center for AI Safety (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a global catastrophe from AI kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: The Center for AI Safety (San Francisco) works to cut the risk of catastrophe from AI through technical research and benchmarks (WMDP, Humanity's Last Exam, circuit breakers), a free compute cluster for outside safety researchers, advocacy and field-building; this model covers all its programmes in 2024 ($7.2M spent; its separate lobbying arm, the CAIS Action Fund, whose gifts aren't tax-deductible, is left out). At the defaults it averts about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, from {{low}} to {{high}} on its plausible range: each dollar is valued as a typical AI project's cut in the forecast risk of an AI catastrophe (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model: its misuse preset for the quarter of the work against misuse, which gives most of the result because Rethink's typical misuse project cuts far more risk per dollar, its misalignment preset for the rest; the shared 5% chance by 2100), with deaths valued like every death and the future lost counted only where you count lives that never start (0% by default). The result moves most with the AI catastrophe chance, Rethink's misuse cut per dollar (a placeholder, ten times either way), the years a cut counts and the discount rate. Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

sections.title: Cost

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

story.sentence: $1,000 funds research, tools and training that cut the risk of AI catastrophe. Every **{1000 / (1000 * donor_cost_share * marginal_vs_past_average * deaths_averted * total_adj / cost_total)|$}** averts **a death** on average.

The share of CAIS's AI spending that is work against misuse. Research names three outputs for 2024 (990 Part III line 4b): WMDP, a benchmark of hazardous knowledge, and circuit breakers, a defence against harmful outputs under attack, are misuse work; Humanity's Last Exam measures capabilities in general. So about half of research ($0.58M of $1.17M), plus perhaps a fifth of the compute cluster's projects (robustness and jailbreak research) ($0.59M), none of advocacy: about $1.2M of $4.9M, 25%, our judgment, 10% to 40%; CAIS publishes no split of its projects.

rows.formula: -((cost_total * ai_cost_share / 1e6 * ai_future_per_million * ai_discounted_years) + (cost_total * bio_cost_share / 1e6 * bio_future_per_million * bio_discounted_years) + (cost_total * nuclear_cost_share / 1e6 * nuclear_future_per_million * nuclear_discounted_years) + (pol_wins * pol_p_success * pol_relative_cut * pol_future_per_year * pol_discounted_years) + (fb_work_dollars / 1e6 * fb_credit_share * fb_future_per_million * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, years_of_impact))) * $lives_added * $animal_dalys_per_person_year_world
rows.explainer: A future kept is also every animal raised to feed it: each future person-year at the suffering of the animals an average person eats in a year today (docs/normalization.md 2.25). Suffering always counts, whatever lives that never start count; the farmed animals' own good days count where you set them to. Held at today's diet: no forecast of what people will eat is used.

rows.label: AI work: how far the typical project's effect applies to it
rows.explainer: How far Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project applies to CAIS's work. Above typical: its outputs are used by the labs and the field: WMDP appears in Google DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Pro model card (Epoch AI's review), Humanity's Last Exam (with Scale AI, nearly 1,000 contributors) is reported by labs for their frontier models (Google's Gemini 2.5 Pro launch: 'a state-of-the-art 18.8%') and CAIS's leaderboard scores the others, and by 2024 over 400 researchers had used the compute cluster for 121 papers with over 5,000 citations (990 Part III line 4a); its 2023 Statement on AI Risk, outside the year, shows its reach. Below typical: the cluster funds outside projects of uneven relevance to catastrophic risk, and Epoch finds WMDP less informative than newer tests. Net 1.2, the family's ceiling (src/engine/templates.ts), our judgment, 0.4 to 1.2; without the ceiling we would put it a little higher.

rows.label: Compute cluster: CAIS's share of the resources behind the papers
rows.explainer: The cluster's papers (121 by 2024 from over 400 researchers, 990 Part III line 4a) are written by outside researchers on CAIS's compute: about 50 to 60 papers a year at a quarter to half a researcher-year each is $1.2M to $7.5M of their time (students at about $100,000, the family's $250,000 for senior staff), about $4M at the middle, against $2.95M of compute, of which $256,598 came back as programme revenue (Part III line 4a), outside money in the cluster. Our judgment, 41% (27% at the most researcher time, 65% at the least).

rows.label: Research: CAIS's share of the resources behind its outputs
rows.explainer: Humanity's Last Exam was made with Scale AI and nearly 1,000 outside experts, WMDP with Scale AI and academic co-authors; circuit breakers and the other papers are mostly CAIS's own staff. Our judgment, 75% (60% to 90%).

rows.label: Advocacy and field-building: CAIS's share of the resources behind them
rows.explainer: The newsletter, media work, textbook and course are CAIS's own; SafeBench's prizes came from Schmidt Sciences and conference workshops use the conferences' venues. Our judgment, 95% (80% to 100%).

rows.label: Weight: healthy years from the AI work (cluster, research, advocacy) (before adjustments)

rows.label: Weight: healthy years from the course (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: The branch's deaths averted in healthy years, plus its future healthy years kept: its share of the value, used to weight the adjustments so each applies to its own branch's value.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: AI work: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Field-building: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: CAIS's share of the resources behind its outputs, branch by branch: the AI work at ai_attribution_share_shared (the compute cluster, whose papers outside researchers write; research, benchmarks made with Scale AI and outside experts; advocacy, CAIS's own), the course at attr_other (CAIS's own). Weighted by each branch's healthy years (w_ai, w_fb), so each share applies to its own branch's value. About {{row:attribution_share}} overall, because the course, whose share is the higher one, carries most of the value.
rows.formula: (w_ai * ai_evidence_adj * ai_counterfactual_adj * ai_attribution_share + w_fb * fb_evidence_adj * fb_counterfactual_adj * fb_attribution_share) / ((w_ai + w_fb) * evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj)

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Whether large funders (a few large donors, in a field big foundations fund heavily) would give less if small donors gave more is the room factor of @next_dollar.center_for_ai_safety (docs/normalization.md 2.10), so it isn't asked again here (one question per adjustment): 1, our judgment, as for every catastrophic-risk model; 0.85 to 1.05 for funging the room factor misses.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of CAIS's work on the risk is measured; the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the chances are forecasts, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the work valued: field-building's other outputs (a NeurIPS workshop with 34 accepted papers, socials for 200+ researchers at ICML and ICLR, SafeBench's 90 benchmark entries), the textbook's readers beyond the course, and safety methods (circuit breakers) used against harms smaller than a catastrophe. 10% (0 to 30%) of the modelled value, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): Humanity's Last Exam is a capability benchmark the labs race on and advertise, and some cluster research (adversarial robustness, representation engineering) also improves capabilities. −5%, our judgment, from −20% to 0. The director's advisory roles at xAI and Scale AI are his own and not CAIS spending.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): WMDP publishes questions on hazardous biology, chemistry and cyber knowledge, but its authors filtered out the sensitive ones and it measures knowledge rather than teaching it. 0, down to −5%, our judgment.
